In this example, we describe how to use splines to model nonlinearities in predictor variables and the generalized additive model.

## Piecewise linear example

```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from patsy import dmatrix

np.random.seed(42)
b0, b1, b2 = 1, 0.5, 35
x = np.arange(1, 101)
y1 = np.random.normal(b0 + b1 * x[:70], 1)
y2 = np.random.normal(b2, 1, 30)
y = np.concatenate([y1, y2])

plt.scatter(x, y)
plt.title("Linear fit to nonlinear data")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
X = sm.add_constant(x)
lin = sm.OLS(y, X).fit()
print(lin.summary())

plt.scatter(x, y)
plt.plot(x, lin.predict(X))
plt.title("Simple linear fit")
plt.show()
```

## Piecewise regression with a knot

```{python}
knot = 70
x_lt = (x < knot).astype(int)
x_ge = (x >= knot).astype(int)
X_pw = np.column_stack([x, x * x_lt, x * x_ge])
X_pw = sm.add_constant(X_pw)
sp = sm.OLS(y, X_pw).fit()
print(sp.summary())

plt.scatter(x, y)
plt.plot(x, sp.predict(X_pw))
plt.title("Piecewise linear fit")
plt.show()
```

## Noisy sine example

```{python}
t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 100)
noise = np.random.normal(0, 5, 100)
y2 = 3 * np.sin(2 * t) + noise

plt.plot(t, y2)
plt.title("Sine curve with Gaussian noise")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
Xt = sm.add_constant(t)
bad_lin = sm.OLS(y2, Xt).fit()
print(bad_lin.summary())

plt.plot(t, y2, label="data")
plt.plot(t, bad_lin.predict(Xt), label="linear fit")
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```

## Cubic spline regression

```{python}
x_spline = dmatrix("bs(t, df=4, include_intercept=True)", {"t": t}, return_type="dataframe")
model_spline = sm.OLS(y2, x_spline).fit()
print(model_spline.summary())

plt.plot(t, y2, label="data")
plt.plot(t, model_spline.predict(x_spline), label="cubic spline fit")
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```
